brief:
A school in Britain has paid compensation to students after threatening to refer them to the Prevent counter-extremism program for wearing Palestinian badges, the Middle East Eye reported. Lion Academy Trust warned the children they would face referral under the government's anti-radicalization scheme for displaying the colours in memory of children killed in Gaza.

The compensation settlement follows backlash over the school's handling of the badges, which students had worn as a memorial. The incident raised concerns about how schools apply Prevent guidelines and whether such measures may chill legitimate political expression among young people.
